dedupe_keys.name: msw optimization multi city nsga ii and topsis framework for allocating municipal solid waste to treatment pathways china

description: This software works out how Chinese cities could split their household waste between landfill, incineration, composting, anaerobic digestion and recycling, and which limit holds each city back from a more circular system. The producers are Tianyong Wu and Chunyuan Zhang of Hubei Polytechnic University, and the package accompanies their manuscript on a multi-city decision-support framework. It uses the NSGA-II genetic algorithm to find trade-offs between cost, emissions and resource recovery, then picks a preferred allocation with entropy-weighted TOPSIS. Coverage is four cities, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Huangshi, under four policy scenarios: a baseline, mandatory waste classification, pricing of externalities, and both combined. The package contains city parameters with notes on their public sources, all experiment scripts including sensitivity, capacity and carbon price sweeps, benchmark logs and the published figures, and is available as a free download from Zenodo, with the code under MIT and data under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, plus a GitHub copy. Caveats: the manuscript was not yet published when read, and parameters are city averages compiled from literature and statistics. Simulation uses: planning treatment capacity mixes and testing classification and pricing policies for municipal waste systems. Related records: SWOLFPy (model-swolfpy) optimises waste systems with life cycle models.
